Q2566343.label: Free National Movement
Q2566343.summary: The Free National Movement (FNM) is a Bahamian conservative and centre-right political party and one of the two principal parties in the country's two-party system. It emerged in the early 1970s from dissidents within the governing Progressive Liberal Party and elements of the former United Bahamian Party, and was initially led by Cecil Wallace-Whitfield. It became the principal alternative to the PLP in the years surrounding Bahamian independence.

Q104853703.label: 1942 Barbadian general election
Q104853703.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 26 January 1942. The result was a victory for the Barbados Electors Association, which won 15 of the 24 seats in the House of Assembly.

Q4858567.label: 1961 Barbadian general election
Q4858567.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 4 December 1961. They were the first held after Barbados was granted full self-government earlier in the year. 24 MPs were elected across twelve two-member constituencies, using the block vote method.

Q6898887.label: 1998 Monegasque general election
Q6898887.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 1 February 1998, with a second round of voting on 8 February. The result was a victory for the National and Democratic Union, which won all 18 seats in the National Council.

Q18518727.label: 2014 Republika Srpska general election
Q18518727.summary: General elections were held in the Republika Srpska entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina on 12 October 2014 as part of the Bosnian general elections.

Q3557575.label: 2003 Cypriot presidential election
Q3557575.desc: 9th election of President of Cyprus Republic
Q3557575.summary: Presidential elections were held in Cyprus on 16 February 2003. The election campaign was dominated by the ongoing negotiations over the Annan Plan for Cyprus. Incumbent President Glafcos Clerides was largely in favour of the plan, while leading opposition candidate Tassos Papadopoulos wanted substantial amendments before he would accept it.

Q17418439.label: 1985 Romanian legislative election
Q17418439.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Romania on 17 March 1985. The Front of Socialist Unity and Democracy (FDUS), dominated by the Romanian Communist Party (PCR) and including other mass organisations, was the only group to contest the elections, and no prospective candidate could run for office without the Front's approval.

Q6016711.label: Turkish presidential election, 1957
Q6016711.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Turkey on November 1, 1957 immediately after the 1957 general elections on October 27. Members of the Grand National Assembly re-elected Celâl Bayar as president. In the same year the 1957 Turkish general election were held.

Q11547847.label: 2013 Lushan earthquake
Q11547847.summary: The Lushan earthquake or Ya'an earthquake occurred at 08:02 Beijing Time on April 20, 2013. The epicenter was located in Lushan County, Ya'an, Sichuan, about 116 km (72 mi) from Chengdu along the Longmenshan Fault in the same province heavily impacted by the 2008 Sichuan earthquake.

Q131725511.label: 2025 N'Djamena attack
Q131725511.summary: On 8 January 2025, an attack was carried out against the presidential palace, known as the Pink Palace, in the Chadian capital N'Djamena by unknown attackers. The 24 attackers attempted to gain entry through a security gate of the presidential palace before being confronted by security forces.

Q2200263.label: Battle of the Strait of Otranto
Q2200263.wiki: Action in the Strait of Otranto
Q2200263.summary: The Action in the Strait of Otranto, also known as the Battle of the Strait of Otranto (1940), was the destruction of an Italian convoy on 12 November 1940 during the Battle of the Mediterranean in the Second World War. It took place in the Strait of Otranto in the Adriatic Sea, between the Royal Navy and the Italian Royal Navy.

Q4871367.label: Battle of Kaiapit
Q4871367.summary: The Battle of Kaiapit was an action fought in 1943 between Australian and Japanese forces in New Guinea during the Markham and Ramu Valley – Finisterre Range campaign of World War II. Following the landings at Nadzab and at Lae, the Allies attempted to exploit their success with an advance into the upper Markham Valley, starting with Kaiapit. The Japanese intended to use Kaiapit to threaten the Allied position at Nadzab, and to create a diversion to allow the Japanese garrison at Lae time to escape.

Q3623111.label: Bombing of Sofia in World War II
Q3623111.wiki: Bombing of Bulgaria in World War II
Q3623111.summary: Bulgaria suffered a series of Allied bombing raids during World War II, from mid 1941 to early 1944. Bulgaria declared war on the United Kingdom and the United States on 13 December 1941. The Southern Italy-based Allied air forces extended the range of their strategic operations to include Bulgaria and other Axis allies in 1943.

Q717511.label: Battle of Sagami Bay
Q717511.desc: 1945 naval battle of the Japanese coast in WWII
Q717511.summary: The Battle of Sagami Bay was a World War II anti-shipping raid off the tip of Bōsō Peninsula on the night of 22 July 1945. It was the last surface action of the war.

Q311495.label: Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi
Q311495.desc: Arab Andalusian physician, surgeon and chemist (936–1013)
aliases: Abū al-Qāsim Khalaf ibn Abbās al-Zahrāwī
Q311495.summary: Abū al-Qāsim Khalaf ibn al-'Abbās al-Zahrāwī al-Ansari, popularly known as al-Zahrawi, Latinised as Albucasis or Abulcasis, was an Arab physician, surgeon and chemist from al-Andalus. He is considered one of the greatest surgeons of the Middle Ages.

Q499911.label: University of Turin
Q499911.summary: The University of Turin is a public research university in the city of Turin, in the Piedmont region of Italy. It is one of the oldest universities in Europe and continues to play an important role in research and training.

Q231111.label: Mary Leakey
Q231111.summary: Mary Douglas Leakey was a British archaeologist and a founding figure in the field of modern paleoanthropology. Her career in African archaeology spanned over 60 years, from the first survey of Olduvai Gorge in 1934 until her passing in 1996, having retired from fieldwork in 1984 after a blood clot left her blind in her left eye. She is credited with the classification of fifteen new animal species, one animal genus, and a series of major discoveries relating to early human evolution in East Africa, specifically the Great Rift Valley.

Q218311.label: François Jacob
Q218311.desc: French biologist and geneticist, winner of the Nobel Prize in 1965
Q218311.summary: François Jacob was a French biologist. He shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Jacques Monod and André Lwoff "for their discoveries concerning genetic control of enzyme and virus synthesis". He and Monod originated the idea that control of enzyme levels in all cells occurs through regulation of transcription. For his work in the French Resistance, he received the Cross of Liberation, the Légion d'honneur and Croix de guerre.

Q2588871.label: Front for Change
Q2588871.summary: Front for Change is a Ukrainian public organization and a former political party in Ukraine, both led by Arseniy Yatsenyuk. The party merged into All-Ukrainian Union "Fatherland" in June 2013.

Q711.label: Mongolia
Q711.summary: Mongolia is a landlocked country in East Asia. It is bordered by Russia to the north and China to the south and covers an area of 1,564,116 square kilometers, making it the 18th-largest country in the world and the second largest landlocked nation after Kazakhstan, as well as the largest landlocked country that does not border an inland sea. With a population of 3.5 million, Mongolia is the world's most sparsely populated sovereign state.
